tour.s: Twenty-two pieces of Belgium sit inside the Netherlands here, and 8 pieces of the Netherlands sit inside those, or inside Belgium proper. The smallest Belgian parcel, H7, is 2,469 square metres. Wikipedia's parcel table has the border running through about 54 homes; in H7 it splits a front door, which has one Belgian and one Dutch house number. Natural Earth draws none of this: at 1:10 million Baarle is just the Netherlands.

Until midnight on 31 July 2015, 102 pieces of India sat inside Bangladesh and 71 pieces of Bangladesh inside India, with 24 counter-enclaves inside those. One, Dahala Khagrabari, was a patch of India, inside Bangladesh, inside India, inside Bangladesh: 6,880 square metres of farmland. The swap gave Bangladesh 111 enclaves and India 51. Only Dahagram-Angarpota is left, joined to Bangladesh by the Tin Bigha Corridor.

Büsingen am Hochrhein is a German village of 7.62 km² surrounded by Switzerland, at its narrowest about 680 m from Germany, and inside the Swiss customs area. Campione d'Italia, an Italian town of 1.6 km² on Lake Lugano, is less than a kilometre from Italy as the crow flies but over 14 km by road through Switzerland. Neither appears in Natural Earth: both are swallowed by Switzerland.

The Treaty of the Pyrenees of 1659 gave France the villages of the Cerdanya valley. Llívia was a town, so it stayed Spanish: 12.84 km² of Spain about 1.6 km inside France. This one is big enough for Natural Earth, which draws it at 13.2 km².

Jungholz is Austrian, but it touches the rest of Austria only at one point, the summit of the Sorgschrofen, where four borders meet. Every road in comes through Germany. Natural Earth, which works at about a kilometre's precision, does not separate it from Austria.

Botswana, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe come within a whisker of meeting here, where the Chobe joins the Zambezi. Wikipedia says all four states agreed in the late 2000s that Botswana and Zambia share a border of about 150 m, so there are two tripoints rather than one quadripoint; the Kazungula Bridge has crossed it since 2021. Natural Earth draws a single point where all four meet: the only quadripoint in its 1:10 million world.

The 49th parallel cut the tip off the Tsawwassen peninsula, leaving a piece of Washington State reachable by land only through 40 km of Canada. Its 1,191 residents (2020) have their own ZIP code. Natural Earth draws it as a separate part of the United States of 5.4 km².

The 1783 Treaty of Paris drew the border from a map that got the Lake of the Woods wrong. The result is the only part of the contiguous United States north of the 49th parallel, reachable by land only through Manitoba. 149 people lived there in 2020.

Russia's westernmost region, the northern half of what was East Prussia, is bordered by Poland, Lithuania and the Baltic Sea. Wikipedia gives it 15,125 km²; Natural Earth's outline, which leaves out the lagoons, measures 13,449 km².
Azerbaijan's exclave of 5,500 km² is bordered by Armenia, Iran and Turkey and has no coast at all. In Natural Earth it is the only exclave that has no coast and touches more than one country.
A strip of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the country's only coast, separates Cabinda from the rest of Angola. Wikipedia gives the province 7,290 km²; Natural Earth draws 6,702 km².

tour.k: Oman, the Emirates, Oman, the Emirates
tour.s: Oman's Musandam peninsula, on the Strait of Hormuz, is cut off from the rest of Oman by the United Arab Emirates. Halfway between the two lies Madha, a piece of Oman surrounded by the Emirates, and inside Madha lies Nahwa, a village of about 40 buildings that belongs to Sharjah. The lines were settled in 1969. Natural Earth draws all three, Nahwa at 7.3 km².

tour.k: Six months French, six months Spanish
tour.s: This river island in the Bidasoa, 6,820 square metres in the condominium table, belongs to both France and Spain. France runs it from 1 August to 31 January, Spain from 1 February to 31 July. Louis XIV met his bride here, the Treaty of the Pyrenees was signed here, and there are no pheasants.

Two lines drawn by Britain, in 1899 and 1902, disagree. Egypt claims the 1899 line and Sudan the 1902 one, because each gives it the larger Halaib Triangle on the Red Sea. That leaves Bir Tawil, 2,060 km² of desert, claimed by neither. Natural Earth draws it as an indeterminate zone, which this page does not count as a country.

tour.k: A border that zigzags round a lighthouse
tour.s: A treaty of 1809 ran the border between Sweden and Finland straight through the middle of this 3.3 hectare skerry. In 1885 Finland built a lighthouse on its highest point, which turned out to be on the Swedish half. In 1985 the line was redrawn as an inverted S of about 480 m, putting the lighthouse in Finland with no net change of territory. It is the smallest sea island shared by two countries, and far too small for Natural Earth.
